summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later lookup; not commentary)

## BOOK 1 of 2: Betty Wales, Junior (Gutenberg #64033, by Margaret Warde / Edith K. Dunton, 1906)

**Premise/Cast.** Junior year at Harding College. Circle from Mrs. Chapin's: Betty Wales (protagonist; yellow curl; "Power Behind the Throne"), Katherine "K." Kittredge (of Kankakee; canvas bag; basketball), Rachel Morrison (steady; tutors conditioned freshmen; moves to little white house off campus; elected junior class president), Roberta Lewis (shy; writes; idolizes Mary), Eleanor Watson (beautiful, snobbish-then-reformed; resigned Dramatic Club last year after a story she signed in the "Argus" that wasn't hers), Helen Chase Adams (roommate; formerly forlorn; "prominent girl" now), Mary Brooks (senior; "Argus" editor; loves practical jokes; Mary-Bird-Club), Dora Carlson (Eleanor's freshman devotee), Madeline Ayres (from "Bohemia, New York"; French/Bohemian; second-self inventor), Nita Reese (roommate-type friend; spread-giver; Hilton House), Miss Ferris (faculty friend), Miss Stuart (registrar/dean), Lucile Merrifield (Betty's freshman cousin, tall, straight hair), Dr. John Elliot Eaton (new associate professor English; brilliant, cold, "ten-minute tests"; rides; never calls roll; later honorary "Merry Heart").
**The B's:** Babbie (Babbie Hildreth; chafing dish with four copper rabbits; "on her smile"), Babe (Babe; Emily Davis mends for her; fake French maid; Nero joke), Bob (Bob Parker; basketball; zoology; toads; ghost prank; night-watchman Henry).
**Others:** Jean Eastman (sharp, Hill-school girl), Christy Mason, Alice Waite, Marion Lawrence (Laurie; "Argus"), Marion Lustig, Emily Davis, Dorothy King (Betty's mentor; "See that everybody has a fair chance"), Frances West (Argus editor-in-chief), Beatrice/Bess Egerton (senior, prominent), Kate Denise, Ethel Hale (Miss Hale; Betty's sister Nan's friend; faculty; later engaged to Dr. Eaton), Mrs. Kent, Miss Andrews, Mrs. Chapin's, Mrs. Tait, Annie (Irish maid), Dr. Hinsdale, Mademoiselle Zita (show), Judge Watson, Jim Watson (Eleanor's brother, Cornell), Nan Wales (Betty's sister), Will Wales (brother), Mr. & Mrs. Wales, "smallest sister" (Little Sister), Paul West (Winsted), Lil Day, Ida Ludwig, Mary's mother.

**Chronology/events:**
1. Ch. I: Betty's new single in Belden House; Mary Brooks arrives; news that Eleanor's Argus scandal leaked. Lucile offered T. Reed's room (Theresa Reed marrying in Philippines). Madeline arrives ("Toss it over, please"). Betty: "Oh, this is the grandest place." Mary: "Don't judge of the ball until it has opened."
2. Ch. II: "The Merry Hearts" club formed at #27 Belden; name suggested by Roberta; no object-meeting rules; Mary: Student Aid Fair idea; pin committee Babe & Roberta; Madeline lecturer on Bohemian spirit. Eleanor kept outside clan.
3. Ch. III: Dr. Eaton's ten-minute test; Madeline writes "Matthew Arnold and the Ten-Minute Test" under invented name **Georgia Ames** (on Helen's sheet). Dance: Bob at Hilton toads; Bob teaches grasshoppers; Madeline plans to propose a new member.
4. Ch. IV: Madeline tells Roberta about Georgia; Georgia "takes English Essayists"; Mary rejects Georgia's "Song of Sleep" poem for Argus; Roberta's novelette; Mary's "I hope she isn't a particular friend"; reveal that Roberta wrote the verse and story.
5. Ch. V: Mushroom party (Madeline's room; oyster-mushroom soup; "inky drippers"/coprinus; puff-balls; meadow mushrooms). Georgia proposed; elected. Betty = "Power Behind the Throne."
6. Ch. VI: Georgia's coming-out: calling cards (Babbie); violets $3.80 (Bob, Westcott senior); Nita's post-card to "Georgiana Arms" from aunt; Mary's Waldorf note; Babe's handkerchief to Dr. Eaton; Helen's forged letter from "Mrs. Erasmus J. Ames"; Eaton replies "Madam."
7. Ch. VII: Dora Carlson crying in library—family's barn fire, father's hand injury; Eleanor pays part of board; Betty suggests Harding Aid; Eleanor suggests Merry Hearts entertain for Dora. Japanese tea (Madeline's one-act plays in fake Japanese; Christy Mason, Professor Jones fooled). Net to Dora ≥$100; Dora made Merry Heart; wears pin from Bob.
8. Ch. VIII: Faculty party at Belden; Dr. Eaton talks to Betty about "mother" note; Betty mistaken for Georgia Ames. Katherine invents Georgia's date; Alice Waite's Tom Alison (Yale); composite picture; Ethel walks home with Eaton.
9. Ch. IX: Eaton summons Georgia; Madeline's "illness" letter: pneumonia, Arizona; Tombstone; Mr. Eaton "Indeed!"; Betty's Christmas.
10. Ch. X: Christmas (Betty's father overworked, West Indies). Tom Alison's letter: John Alison (older brother, Eaton's college chum) sent picture to Eaton with love-note from "Georgia." Betty confesses to Eaton in office; he laughs; wants honorary membership; "A great deal depends on this year."
11. Ch. XI: Janitor & clock-tower; Bob's ghost prank; Dr. Eaton honorary member; Miss Stuart; Miss Case. Ethel crying at window; Nassau invitation from Betty's father (letter from Nassau, B.I.). Chaperon Ethel Hale. Members: Babbie, Babe, Bob, Betty, Mary, Helen, Roberta, Madeline, Eleanor (later).
12. Ch. XII: Eleanor invited; fire in Main Building library; Bob leads girls; Henry the night-watchman ("You done noble"); extra week in June.
13. Ch. XIII: Departure (Rachel, Katherine, Nita, Dora at station). Dr. Eaton on board. Ethel seasick. Nassau: launch; Mr. Wales; Betty's parents; divers for pennies; Hilton annex; Fort; Philip Charles Augustus Smith.
14. Ch. XIV: Grant's Town; roses threepence; orange grove; Easter tree (Roberta idea); orange-rolling for ten urchins; Dr. Eaton and Ethel lost.
15. Ch. XV: Hog Island; Betty nearly drowns; Dr. Eaton saves her; Ethel says "I can't thank you enough, John."
16. Ch. XVI: Blackbeard's Well; Eleanor's Prom escort Jim; Eleanor withdraws from Dramatic Club.
17. Ch. XVII: Helen elected Argus editor; Eleanor's supper; Eleanor elected to Merry Hearts.
18. Ch. XVIII: Ethel's al fresco; Ethel engaged to Eaton (since last fall; he'd given her a year). Dress reform: simple ushers' dresses; Babbie's princess dress; Lotta Gardner; Rachel.
19. Ch. XIX: Dr. Eaton leaving; $50,000 gift to college for dress reform; Betty applauded; Georgia "found" as entrance candidate.

**Key quotes:** "Hello, Betty Wales. Please amuse me." / "Toss it over, please" / "Georgia Ames doesn't cut" / "Power Behind the Throne" / "Indeed!" (Eaton) / "I can't thank you enough, John."

## BOOK 2 of 2: Betty Wales, Sophomore (Gutenberg #6432, by Margaret Warde / Edith K. Dunton, 1905)

**Cast additions:** Helen Chase Adams (roommate; gym; basketball; song writer), Theresa Reed ("T. Reed," Helen's roommate later), Lucile Merrifield (cousin), Dora Carlson (Ohio farm; Market Street; 50 Market St.; waitress at Mrs. Tait's), Nettie Dwight (Market Street girl), Mrs. Bryant (kitchen), Eleanor Watson (Hilton House, extra-priced corner single; story in "Argus" copied from "The Quiver"), Jean Eastman (Hill girl; cousin Polly Eastman), Paul West (Winsted), Beatrice/Bess Egerton (senior, Dramatic Club president, exchange editor), Frances West (Argus editor-in-chief, poet), Dorothy King (Argus business manager, senior class president, Students' Commission), Richard Blake (editor of "The Quiver," NY; Paris friend of Madeline; "Dick"), Christy Mason (Students' Commission member; away for mother's illness), Lucy Merrifield (class president), Miss Ferris, Miss Raymond (theme course), Miss Stuart, Miss Mills (Lit II), Miss Andrews, Professor White (Napoleon), Professor Lawrence, Dr. Hinsdale, Mrs. Cass (Belden matron), Ida Ludwig (pianist), Babbie, Babe, Bob (B's), Madeline Ayres (class secretary; Bohemia; languages; Bengali), Nita Reese (birthday Feb 9), Mary Brooks (senior; "Argus"; hair-raising), Marion Lawrence (Laurie), Marion Lustig, Emily Davis, Alice Waite, Katherine Kittredge, Rachel Morrison (Clio), Roberta Lewis (Boston cousin; Nan's Cleveland), Will & Nan Wales, Ethel Hale, Miss Hale ("little sister" = Betty), Lotta Gardner, Miss Ray, Sara Westervelt (freshman), Laura Perkins, Kate Denise, Polly Eastman, Mrs. Mulvaney (washwoman), Mr. Tom Alison (no—Tom is in book 1), Mrs. Alison (Bob's matron), Henry (watchman, book 1).

**Introduction facts:** Nine girls at Mrs. Chapin's freshman year; Mary Brooks sophomore (book 1 facts).

**Chronology:**
1. Ch. I: Moving in, sophomore year. Betty's single; green lizard; Eleanor returns softened; Rachel off campus (white house); Madeline Ayres introduces herself ("Bohemia, New York," languages, Bengali). "Don't put that green vase there." Nita's birthday, B's on 4th floor.
2. Ch. II: Sophomore reception: Polly Eastman ill; Eleanor takes Dora Carlson (left-over freshman, Market St.). Dora's Cinderella night; violets; Dora to Hilton for Sunday dinner. Jean sneers.
3. Ch. III: Madeline's "Republican parade" (Mary, Nita defeated candidate, Roosevelt/Fairbanks). Hallowe'en. Helen takes gym to be "marvel of grace." Helen's ambition to write.
4. Ch. IV: Eleanor writes story; Eleanor's theme "The...," reads to class by Miss Raymond; Dorothy King demands it for Argus; Eleanor "I can't let the 'Argus' use my story."
5. Ch. V: Harding Aid "Show" (Madeline; Mary; Emily Davis; Happy Family; "Animal Song"; Animal Fair play). $50 for Aid.
6. Ch. VI: Miss Hale/Betty walk; Nan & Will visit (Will, Mary, Dorothy King, Eleanor not caught); Betty dinner at Cuyler's refused by Eleanor (Beatrice Egerton); "Do you see any use in ambition?"
7. Ch. VII: Roberta to Cleveland for Christmas; Mrs. Wales; midyears; tea with Katherine & Rachel; Katherine vs Eleanor ("lady Eleanor").
8. Ch. VIII: Nita's birthday spread; Dramatic Club elections: Bob, Eleanor, Marion Lustig, a fourth; Eleanor elected (Beatrice rushing her); Eleanor's "footless little story."
9. Ch. IX: Basketball; Betty appointed to Students' Commission (Christy away); Miss Ferris tea ("cooperation"); Mary's hair-raising (mother); Marion Lawrence's letter for Frances West on zoology bulletin board.
10. Ch. X: Dorothy at Argus sanctum with Frances & Beatrice; letter from Richard Blake, "The Quiver" (Feb 2): Eleanor's story copied from November "Quiver." Reply sent; Blake's second letter: "I blame neither you nor your associates."
11. Ch. XI: Dorothy ill; sends Betty to NY; Betty's problem; Madeline's advice ("medal" for stolen design); Madeline knows (read "Quiver" at father's). Napoleon written lesson.
12. Ch. XII: Eleanor's reconciliation with Betty at Betty's room; Jim visits (Feb weekend); Jim asks Betty to walk; Betty decides to go to NY.
13. Ch. XIII: Blizzard; train late; Davidson Hotel (matron); Betty meets Richard Blake at "Quiver" office (young cynical editor; "Let us make a fair start"); Blake lectures on Dramatic Club stage; Betty returns at 11:30 p.m.; Helen: "did it take out the curl?"; grippe; teams chosen; Babbie is sub-centre.
14. Ch. XIV: Katherine's show invitation; Eleanor's dinner with Miss Ferris & Blake; Blake meets Madeline ("Dick"); Dorothy: Blake asks Eleanor "Would you be willing to risk one thoroughly dishonest student?"; Blake's lecture "Tendencies of the Modern Drama"; Eleanor writes new story (western life, from Jim).
15. Ch. XV: Basketball game; Helen's song wins; Eleanor's song rejected (Jean on committee); Beatrice insinuates to Jean; Betty interrupts. Students' Commission key to Christy. Betty's idea to get Eleanor confiding in Miss Ferris.
16. Ch. XVI: Dora's sugaring-off at Mrs. Bryant's kitchen (Nettie Dwight, cousins); fortunes; Eleanor reads Dora's "soul of truth" fortune with irony; Beatrice's remark.
17. Ch. XVII: May-day little girls; Eleanor & Miss Ferris in Paradise; Eleanor confesses; resolves to resign Dramatic Club; Betty, Madeline, Mary catch them.
18. Ch. XVIII: Betty elected Dramatic Club (pins); Eleanor resigns; Dramatic Club accepts resignation one year; Bob loses Eleanor's basketball song; Eleanor & Betty.
19. Ch. XIX: Eleanor gives up corner room for Dora; Helen & T. Reed to room together; Betty to be Dorothy's successor (Dorothy leaving); Madeline's washwoman; "Here's to junior year!" (END).

**Key quotes:** "Don't put that green vase there." / "Oh, Betty Wales, what's your hurry?" / "Let us make a fair start" (Blake) / "Would you be willing to risk one thoroughly dishonest student" / "Never mind that now" (Betty) / "Here's to junior year!"
